_readme: Copy this file to mic.config.json and edit it. Every key is optional — an empty {} boots a
working Microphone. Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored.
Full explanations: README.md (setup) and docs/SECURITY.md (before you touch `foreman`).
_port: The port the Mic listens on, loopback only. Override at runtime with MIC_PORT.
_workspaceRoot: The tree your lines work in, and the ONLY tree the file viewer will serve from.
Relative paths resolve against the folder this server lives in. The default, '..',
means: clone the-microphone into the project you want to run, and it just works.
_claudeBin: Path to the claude binary. Leave empty to auto-detect: CLAUDE_BIN, then `claude` on PATH,
then the VS Code extension binary on Windows. Whatever it lands on is printed at boot.
_credentialsDir: Where the approval word and any armed-turn secrets live. Deliberately OUTSIDE the workspace,
so no line can reach them by walking the tree and no commit can ever carry them.
_models: Which models exist, what your spoken words map to, and what each standing seat is born on.
`known` is a whitelist: an id that is not in it is REJECTED at open time rather than
silently spawning a line on a model that does not exist.
PIN SITE: the same ids appear in the two <select> blocks in index.html.
_folders: Optional shortcuts for the 'where it works' picker when you open a line by hand.
The workspace root is always offered and is the right answer almost every time.
Leave this empty unless you genuinely run lines rooted in separate repos.
_cockpit: The Cockpit tab renders plain files you keep in your workspace — it writes nothing, ever.
Name the ones you keep and it renders them; leave a key out and that panel is simply absent.
The formats these parsers expect are written down in docs/COCKPIT.md. They are ordinary
markdown you would keep by hand anyway — no format is invented for the Cockpit's benefit.
Paths are relative to workspaceRoot. Absolute paths are refused.
_foreman: ⚠ READ docs/SECURITY.md BEFORE ENABLING THIS. The Foreman is one line that can be handed
elevated helpers for exactly one turn, when your reply carries the approval word.
The word is a PRESENCE CEREMONY — proof a human is at the keyboard approving — and it is NOT
a boundary against a hostile line: every line runs as the same OS user, so any line can read
the word file. Never put a destructive action behind the word alone.
OFF by default. `helpers` lists filenames in helpers/ (see examples/README.md for the pattern);
`secrets` maps an environment variable to a filename inside credentialsDir, handed to the armed
spawn only, for that one turn. Both ship empty on purpose.
